data.title: Suspicious debt collection demand from EuroClaim (€287.40)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 by 6 August 2026 for an alleged phone-concluded prize-draw subscription, threatening seizure and a criminal complaint. The letter shows several strong scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter looks like a scam or at least a very aggressive, dubious claim. It has a 72-hour deadline, threats of account seizure and criminal charges, a generic salutation, added fees, and payment to a private person's account in Lithuania. A real collector would not demand payment to an individual's "trust account". Do not pay under pressure. Check whether you ever had this subscription. Consider asking a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer, and you may report it to the police. Only a court can order an account seizure, and only after a formal court process. Keep the letter as evidence.

warnings: Payment is demanded to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual (A. Petrauskas), not a company or collection agency account.
Extreme 72-hour deadline and threats of seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal complaint are typical pressure tactics.
The letter uses a generic salutation ('Sehr geehrte/r Schuldner/in') and says objection is pointless, which is not true.
Fees (collection costs €84 and a €24 account fee) are unexplained and may be unjustified.
The stated deadline of 6 August 2026 has already passed; do not pay in a hurry, and verify the claim independently.
